note: WP-25: cultural rules applied when a film is localised (gesture swaps, which a film's i18n file can turn off with "rules_off") and words a locale's reviewers look at before posting (flags only, never changed automatically). Rules name languages (ISO 639-1) and regions (ISO 3166-1); they are defaults for review, not statements about people, and each says why. Sources: common localisation and cross-cultural communication guidance on gestures (e.g. Axtell, Gestures: The Do's and Taboos of Body Language Around the World, 1998) and on religious dietary norms; extend or correct them as reviewers advise.

rules.why: Giving, pointing or waving with the left hand reads as impolite in much of the Middle East, North Africa and South Asia; the same gesture with the right hand does not.
Pointing at someone with the index finger reads as rude in parts of South-East Asia (an open hand or the thumb is used instead).
Alcohol and pork are not consumed by many viewers for religious reasons; showing them casually can put an audience off.
Beef is not eaten by many viewers (Hindu tradition); a casual beef dish may be better swapped.
Dogs kept indoors as close companions are seen differently by some Muslim audiences; worth a look in family scenes.
Four sounds like 'death' in Mandarin, Japanese and Korean; reviewers may prefer it not to be a lucky or featured number.
A thumbs-up is rude in parts of West Africa, the Middle East and South America; check gestures drawn into props or overlays.
